description: Design system regulations for automotive in-vehicle infotainment (IVI) and head unit interfaces, based on NHTSA guidelines, ISO standards, and driver distraction research.

references.name: NHTSA Visual-Manual Driver Distraction Guidelines
references.description: National Highway Traffic Safety Administration guidelines for reducing driver distraction from in-vehicle electronic devices.

references.name: ISO 15005 - Dialogue Management
references.description: International standard for ergonomic principles of dialogue management in transport information and control systems.

references.name: ISO 15008 - Road Vehicle Displays
references.description: Specifications for presentation of information on road vehicle displays.

references.name: Android Automotive OS Design Guidelines
references.description: Google's design guidelines for Android Automotive OS applications.

references.name: Apple CarPlay Human Interface Guidelines
references.description: Apple's guidelines for designing CarPlay applications.

references.name: ISO 26262 Functional Safety
references.description: Functional safety standard for road vehicles.

regulations.title: Driver Distraction Prevention
regulations.description: In-vehicle interfaces must minimize driver distraction in compliance with NHTSA guidelines and international driver distraction standards.

rules.requirement: Any single glance at the display must not require more than 2 seconds of visual attention. Tasks requiring multiple glances must be completable within a total of 12 seconds.
rules.rationale: NHTSA research shows glances longer than 2 seconds significantly increase crash risk.

rules.requirement: Any driver-initiated task must be completable within 12 seconds of total glance time or must be blocked while the vehicle is in motion.
rules.rationale: The NHTSA 12-second total glance time rule is the accepted standard for in-vehicle tasks.

rules.requirement: Complex interactions (text input, browsing lists longer than 6 items, video playback) must be disabled when the vehicle speed exceeds 5 mph (8 km/h). A clear message must explain why the feature is unavailable.
rules.rationale: Complex visual-manual tasks while driving are the leading cause of distraction-related crashes.

rules.requirement: Tasks must require no more than 3 steps (taps, swipes, or voice commands) to complete common actions while driving. Frequently used functions must be accessible in 1-2 interactions.
rules.rationale: Fewer interaction steps mean shorter eyes-off-road time and reduced cognitive load.

rules.requirement: Scrollable lists presented to the driver while the vehicle is in motion must not exceed 6 visible items per screen without paging or voice-assisted navigation.
rules.rationale: NHTSA guidelines limit list browsing complexity to reduce visual search time.

regulations.title: In-Vehicle Typography
regulations.description: Text in automotive displays must be readable at a glance under all driving conditions.

rules.requirement: Text on the center display must have a minimum character height of 6.4mm (approximately 18pt at standard viewing distance). Critical information (speed, warnings) must use at least 8mm character height.
rules.rationale: ISO 15008 specifies minimum character heights for legibility at driver viewing distances.

rules.requirement: Fonts must be sans-serif with open apertures and generous x-height. Recommended fonts include Roboto, San Francisco, Noto Sans, or purpose-built automotive fonts. Decorative or condensed fonts are prohibited.
rules.rationale: Sans-serif fonts with clear letterforms are most legible during brief glances at distance.

rules.requirement: On-screen text presented to the driver must be limited to essential information. Labels must not exceed 3 words. Notification messages must not exceed 2 lines of text.
rules.rationale: Drivers cannot safely read long text; information must be conveyed in the shortest possible form.

rules.requirement: Scrolling, animated, or auto-updating text must not be displayed on screens visible to the driver while the vehicle is in motion.
rules.rationale: Moving text requires sustained visual attention incompatible with safe driving.

regulations.title: Automotive Color System
regulations.description: Colors in automotive displays must ensure visibility under all ambient lighting conditions and convey safety-critical information reliably.

rules.requirement: Displays must maintain a minimum contrast ratio of 3:1 in direct sunlight and must automatically adjust brightness for night driving to prevent glare. Night mode must use a dark background with light text.
rules.rationale: Automotive displays must be readable in extreme lighting conditions from bright sun to darkness.

rules.requirement: Red must be reserved exclusively for critical/danger alerts (engine failure, collision warning). Amber/yellow for caution/warnings. Green for normal/confirmed status. Blue for informational displays. These mappings must never be overridden.
rules.rationale: ISO 2575 and automotive industry conventions establish universal color meanings that drivers expect.

rules.requirement: In night mode, the display must limit bright colors and use a predominantly dark palette. White backgrounds are prohibited. Maximum display brightness must be automatically capped to prevent glare adaptation loss.
rules.rationale: Bright displays at night cause pupil constriction and temporary blindness when looking back at the road.

rules.requirement: Safety-critical information must never rely on color alone. Shapes (triangle for warning, circle for prohibition), icons, and text labels must always accompany color coding.
rules.rationale: Up to 8% of male drivers have color vision deficiency; safety info must be perceivable by all.

rules.requirement: Display color temperature and brightness must automatically adapt based on ambient light sensors. Manual brightness override must always be available.
rules.rationale: Static brightness causes either washed-out displays in daylight or blinding glare at night.

regulations.title: In-Vehicle Display Layout
regulations.description: Display layouts must prioritize safety-critical information and minimize visual search time.

rules.requirement: The display must be organized into priority zones: Zone 1 (top/center) for driving-critical information (speed, navigation turn, warnings); Zone 2 (middle) for active task content; Zone 3 (bottom/periphery) for status indicators and secondary controls.
rules.rationale: Zoned layouts reduce visual search time by placing critical information where drivers look first.

rules.requirement: Touch targets must be at least 12.7mm x 12.7mm (approximately 48dp) with at least 6mm spacing between adjacent targets. Frequently used controls should be at least 20mm x 20mm.
rules.rationale: Larger touch targets compensate for vehicle vibration and the difficulty of precise touch while driving.

rules.requirement: Navigation and speed information must be displayed in the driver's primary line of sight (instrument cluster or HUD) in addition to the center display.
rules.rationale: Reducing the angle between road view and display reduces eyes-off-road time.

rules.requirement: Core navigation elements (home, back, media controls) must remain in fixed positions regardless of the active application or driving mode.
rules.rationale: Consistent control placement allows drivers to build muscle memory and reduce glance time.

regulations.title: Driver Interaction Patterns
regulations.description: Interaction patterns must be optimized for the driving context where visual and manual attention are limited.

rules.requirement: All frequently used functions (navigation destination, phone calls, media selection, climate control) must be accessible via voice commands as an alternative to touch.
rules.rationale: Voice control allows drivers to keep their eyes on the road and hands closer to the wheel.

rules.requirement: Steering wheel controls and physical knobs/buttons must be supported for core functions (volume, track skip, call accept/reject, voice activation). Physical controls must take priority over touchscreen equivalents.
rules.rationale: Physical controls provide haptic feedback and can be operated without looking.

rules.requirement: Touch gestures must be limited to tap, swipe, and pinch-to-zoom (for maps only while parked). Multi-finger gestures, long presses, and complex gesture sequences are prohibited while driving.
rules.rationale: Complex gestures require visual attention to perform and verify, increasing distraction.

rules.requirement: Every driver interaction must produce immediate multi-modal feedback: visual change plus audio confirmation or haptic response within 250ms.
rules.rationale: Drivers who don't receive immediate feedback will look at the display to verify their action.

regulations.title: In-Vehicle Navigation UI
regulations.description: Navigation and map displays must provide clear guidance while minimizing driver distraction.

rules.requirement: Turn-by-turn navigation must display: a large directional arrow, distance to next maneuver in driver's preferred unit, street name, and lane guidance. Instructions must be readable in under 2 seconds.
rules.rationale: Navigation instructions are safety-critical and must be instantly comprehensible.

rules.requirement: While the vehicle is in motion, maps must automatically reduce detail level: hiding non-essential POIs, simplifying road networks, and enlarging the current route. Full detail maps are available only when parked.
rules.rationale: Detailed maps require extended visual search time that is unsafe while driving.

rules.requirement: Estimated time of arrival, remaining distance, and current road name/speed limit must be persistently visible during active navigation without requiring any interaction.
rules.rationale: Drivers frequently need route status information and should not have to tap to see it.

regulations.title: Automotive Alerts and Notifications
regulations.description: Alerts and notifications must be delivered through appropriate channels based on urgency and driving context.

rules.requirement: Alerts must be categorized into three tiers: Critical (collision, system failure) with visual + audio + haptic delivery; Warning (low fuel, traffic) with visual + audio; Information (message received, weather) with brief visual notification only.
rules.rationale: Tiered alerting prevents alert fatigue while ensuring critical alerts are impossible to miss.

rules.requirement: Non-critical notifications must be queued and batched during active navigation maneuvers. No more than one non-critical notification may be displayed per 30-second interval.
rules.rationale: Frequent notifications during critical driving moments increase accident risk.

rules.requirement: Critical audio alerts must be played at a volume that is audible over the current media and road noise. Non-critical alerts must respect the user's notification volume setting. Alert sounds must be distinct and not resemble common environmental sounds.
rules.rationale: Inaudible critical alerts or annoying frequent alerts both compromise driver safety.

rules.requirement: Non-critical alerts must auto-dismiss after 5 seconds. Critical alerts must persist until acknowledged by the driver via a single tap or voice command.
rules.rationale: Persistent non-critical alerts distract; auto-dismissing critical alerts may be missed.

regulations.title: Automotive Component Standards
regulations.description: UI components for automotive displays must be designed for the unique constraints of the driving environment.

rules.requirement: The media player must display: current track/station info (max 2 lines), album art (optional), and large play/pause/skip controls. Controls must be operable via touch, steering wheel buttons, and voice.
rules.rationale: Media is the most frequently used in-vehicle function and must be instantly controllable.

rules.requirement: Climate controls must display current temperature, target temperature, fan speed, and air distribution with intuitive visual indicators. Temperature adjustment must be possible in single-tap increments.
rules.rationale: Climate control is a frequent driver need that must not require complex interaction.

rules.requirement: Incoming call screens must display caller name/number prominently with large accept/reject buttons. During calls, the interface must minimize to a small persistent indicator showing call duration and a prominent end-call button.
rules.rationale: Phone interaction while driving must be as brief and simple as possible.

rules.requirement: Rear/surround camera views must display trajectory guidelines, distance indicators, and obstacle highlighting. Camera views must activate automatically when reverse gear is engaged.
rules.rationale: Camera-assisted parking is a safety feature that must provide clear spatial guidance.

regulations.title: Automotive Accessibility
regulations.description: In-vehicle systems must be accessible to drivers and passengers with various abilities.

rules.requirement: Voice control must support natural language input (not just exact command phrases), provide voice readback of on-screen content, and allow complete hands-free operation of all non-visual features.
rules.rationale: Drivers with motor impairments may rely entirely on voice for vehicle controls.

rules.requirement: Display brightness, contrast, text size, and color scheme must be user-adjustable. A high-contrast mode must be available that exceeds standard contrast ratios by at least 50%.
rules.rationale: Driver visual capabilities vary widely; adjustable displays serve all users safely.

rules.requirement: All visual alerts and notifications must have an audio equivalent that can be enabled in accessibility settings. Screen reader support must be available for passenger-side infotainment.
rules.rationale: Drivers with visual impairments may not see visual-only alerts.

regulations.title: Automotive Motion and Animation
regulations.description: Motion and animation in automotive displays must enhance usability without creating distraction.

rules.requirement: Non-essential animations (decorative transitions, loading spinners, parallax effects) must be disabled while the vehicle is in motion. Only functional animations (screen transitions, progress indicators) are permitted.
rules.rationale: Decorative animations attract driver attention away from the road without functional benefit.

rules.requirement: Screen transitions must complete within 300ms. If content is loading, the new screen frame must appear immediately with content populating progressively.
rules.rationale: Slow transitions cause drivers to stare at the display waiting for the result.

rules.requirement: Map scrolling and zoom animations must run at a minimum of 30fps to prevent motion sickness for passengers and maintain spatial orientation for the driver.
rules.rationale: Choppy map animations disrupt spatial understanding and can cause passenger discomfort.
